question: When can a scoped cache response remain sufficient at use, and where do TTL/metadata/source-truth assumptions fail?

requirements.required: Tenant/resource/task/source binding remains applicable at the receiving boundary
I requires the declared response/effect/receipt; M requires an explicit meaningful admitted fallback or continuity outcome
Current authority/evidence/epoch and useful horizon are checked at use where material
Typing, identity, TTL, acknowledgement or notification alone does not establish business completion or current truth
Candidate trace is sealed before private grading; actual state/effect is inspected separately
Selected costs are trace-accounted; M admission precedes Type1; Type2 causal rules and exclusions are explicit
An ANSWER must retain a qualified source/tenant/generation binding; an empty returned binding cannot establish I

assumptions: trusted current source/authority assertions except declared source-fault diagnostics
Stage_B_entry: Candidate package is explicit and frozen; a B successor still needs a declared architecture, requirement-to-realization matrix, selected verification vectors/mutations and a new pre-execution contract
